previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was admitted following transfer from an outside hospital for management of a severe flare. She presented with epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and constipation, but no fever or respiratory symptoms. She was maintained on NPO status with TPN and IV hydromorphone initially, then transitioned to oral pain medications and full liquids as her symptoms improved. Imaging showed no evidence of acute pancreatitis or obstruction, though a right middle lobe lung opacity was noted, likely due to prior aspiration. Constipation was managed with laxatives, and she had a bowel movement before discharge. She was discharged home on TPN, oral hydromorphone, antiemetics, and stool softeners, with follow-up arranged with her specialist and primary care provider.
